title: Minimum Moves to Spread Stones Over Grid
summary: Given a 3x3 grid with exactly 9 stones distributed among its cells, determine the least number of moves needed to ensure each cell contains exactly one stone.
statement: Given a 3x3 grid with exactly 9 stones distributed among its cells, determine the least number of moves needed to ensure each cell contains exactly one stone. In a single move, a stone can be transferred to an adjacent cell.
constraints: grid is exactly 3x3, contains nonnegative counts, and totals nine stones.
One move transfers one stone across one shared side.
Return the minimum moves until every cell contains exactly one stone.
hints: Each surplus stone must be assigned to one currently empty cell.
Use a bitmask of filled empty cells and add Manhattan assignment costs one surplus at a time.
Transition every state by assigning the next surplus to each unfilled target.
Every valid final placement is a bijection between surplus stones and empty cells; the DP enumerates all such bijections and minimizes their exact movement costs.
editorial: Every valid final placement is a bijection between surplus stones and empty cells; the DP enumerates all such bijections and minimizes their exact movement costs.

tests.explanation: The surplus bottom-middle stone travels three grid edges to the empty top-right cell.
Assigning the four surplus stones to the four empty cells costs four moves.
